page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of 1200 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware graphics acceleration is not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable multi-threaded throughput balanced by modest single-threaded compute metrics. The instance achieved 27,102.96 in stress-ng multi-core testing, while single-core performance registered in the lower quartile at 1,286.38. Similarly, single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression speeds placed in the lower tier, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered an average rating of 66.82 GB/sec. Geekbench 6 results reflect consistent mid-tier execution with a single-core score of 1,185 and a multi-core score of 10,191. Memory subsystem tests recorded uncached read throughput of 108.78 GB/sec and write throughput of 47.88 GB/sec.

The presence of 1200 GB of attached NVMe storage, combined with 256 GB of RAM, provides strong density for workloads constrained by I/O latency and memory capacity. Qualitative cost efficiency favors large transactional sets where local caching avoids additional managed block storage fees. However, applications bound strictly to single-core execution speed or high-throughput LLM generation will experience architectural limitations, as indicated by a poor prompt processing rate of 3.91 tokens/sec on 70B parameter models.

Amazon Web Services r5dn.8xlarge is well suited for memory-intensive production databases, in-memory caches like Redis, distributed data analytics engines, and real-time transaction processing systems that benefit from direct NVMe instance storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 256 GB of DDR4 system memory, 1200 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage, and 25 Gbps baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations indicate stable mid-tier multi-threaded execution, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,191 and 26.38 million Redis SET operations per second, counterbalanced by lower single-threaded metrics. The bundled high-speed NVMe storage and generous 8 GB of RAM per vCPU establish high operational efficiency for disk-caching and memory-heavy systems without requiring external volume overhead. This hardware configuration is suitable for hosting enterprise in-memory databases, Redis deployments, transactional processing pipelines, and data analytics tasks requiring dense local storage and rapid memory access.
